summary.text: Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great, was the founder of the Achaemenid Empire and came from Persis; he lived from about 600 to 530 BC.
He defeated the Median Empire, then conquered Lydia and the Neo-Babylonian Empire, building what soon became the largest empire in history at the time.
He was known for tolerating the customs and religions of conquered peoples, and Judaism exalts him for freeing the Jews from the Babylonian captivity.

facts.label: Tomb
facts.value: Pasargadae, revered by millions in modern Iran

items.prompt: A conquered people asks to keep its own customs and gods. What was Cyrus's habitual policy toward such peoples?

options.label: Forced adoption of Persian gods
Tolerance for their customs and religions
Moving them to his capital
Taxing them more heavily for it

items.explain: To the Greeks he was renowned for his habitual policy of tolerance for peoples' customs and religions in the lands he conquered.

items.prompt: Jews held in Babylonian captivity came under Persian rule after Cyrus took Babylon. What did his Edict of Restoration allow?

options.label: Staying in Babylon under Persian protection
Settling in Persis near his capital
Joining his army against the Massagetae
Returning to Judah and rebuilding Jerusalem's Temple

items.explain: He freed the Jewish people from the Babylonian captivity, and his efforts enabled their return and the completion of the Second Temple.

items.prompt: A realm this huge needs a way to govern distant lands. What system did Cyrus help develop?

options.label: A central administration at his capital to govern the satraps
Direct rule of every province by the king in person
Self-governing cities that sent only soldiers
Rule by Median generals alone

items.explain: He was influential in developing a central administration at his capital to govern the Achaemenid Empire's satraps.

items.prompt: Accounts differ on how Cyrus died. What does Xenophon say?

options.label: He fell fighting the Massagetae by the Syr Darya
He died at Babylon after the city fell
He did not die fighting but returned to Pasargadae
He was killed by his son Cambyses II

items.explain: One account has him dying in battle with the Massagetae, but Xenophon says he did not die fighting and returned to the capital, Pasargadae.

items.prompt: Later Persian empires looked back at Cyrus's era. How did they view it?

options.label: As a failure to avoid repeating
As a myth with no real history
As a time of foreign rule they resented
With deference, as the ideal example to emulate

items.explain: Future Persian empires often viewed the Achaemenid era with deference and as the ideal example to emulate.

items.prompt: After conquering Lydia and then the Neo-Babylonian Empire, which regions did Cyrus control as a result?

options.label: Egypt and Nubia
Anatolia and the Fertile Crescent
Greece and Scythia
Cyrenaica and the Balkans

items.explain: Conquering Lydia and the Neo-Babylonian Empire gave him control of Anatolia and the Fertile Crescent respectively; Egypt and Nubia fell later under Cambyses II.
